alerts.disclaimer: These notes only describe what your own entries say — they are not a medical assessment. If you are worried, call your paediatric practice; when in doubt, rather once too early.

fewWetToday.detail: About six a day is the usual guide. A single day below that is mostly harmless; several in a row are worth asking about.
fewWetToday.title: Only {n} wet nappy today | Only {n} wet nappies today

intakeDown.detail: {amount} ml against the usual {average} ml. A single day varies often; if it stays that way for several days, it is worth asking.
intakeDown.title: {percent} % less to drink yesterday

intakeUp.detail: {amount} ml against the usual {average} ml. In hot weather or during a growth spurt that is perfectly normal.
intakeUp.title: {percent} % more to drink yesterday

longSinceFeed.detail: Usually it is about {typical} hours. Young infants who skip a feed and are hard to wake should be seen by a doctor.
longSinceFeed.title: Last bottle {hours} hours ago

noWetDiaper.detail: Wet nappies are the most reliable sign that enough is getting through.
noWetDiaper.detailTypical: Usually there is one about every {hours} hours. Wet nappies are the most reliable sign that enough is getting through.
noWetDiaper.title: No wet nappy for {hours} hours

app.description: Track feeds, nappies, sleep and development

boot.resetHint: Resetting only clears the copy on this device. All entries stay on the server and on the other devices.

charts.diaperHeatmapCaption: Nappies of the last {days} days by hour
charts.empty: As soon as a few feeds are recorded, the charts appear here.
charts.growthLegend: Grey lines: WHO percentiles P3, P15, P50 (solid), P85 and P97.
charts.noMeasurements: No measurements yet. Under “History → Add entry” you can record weight and length — for example the values from the last check-up.
charts.percentile: Currently on percentile {n} — {n} of 100 children the same age are {comparison}.
charts.percentileNote: What matters is not the single value but whether the curve follows its band. A child on percentile 20 is healthy as long as they stay on percentile 20.
charts.rhythmLead: One dot per feed, the size stands for the amount. Midnight is at the top and the bottom — that makes the night-time band visible, which thins out over the months.
charts.sameAsLastWeek: about the same as last week
charts.title: Charts

child.dueDateHint: The developmental leaps count from this date, not from birth. For a premature baby the timeline would otherwise be off by weeks. May be left empty.
child.name: Name
child.sexHint: Determines which WHO growth charts are used for comparison.

colicDrops.hint: e.g. simeticone — given in the bottle

spatUp.hint: Not counted towards the daily total

invalid.one: One entry could not be synced
invalid.text: The values are out of range. Please tap the entry and correct it — after that it syncs automatically.

intake.note: A rough guide: about one sixth of body weight in milk per day, before solids. How much she actually needs she decides herself — hunger and fullness cues say more than any number.
intake.praiseUsual: Already as much as on an ordinary day.

join.title: Welcome
join.wrongToken: The invite link is not right. Please ask the other parent.

leap.disclaimer: The leap weeks come from a popular but scientifically contested model. Take them as a rough pointer, not a timetable — every child has their own.
leap.title: Leap {n}: {name}

1.description: The senses wake up. Many babies seem more easily startled and want to be carried more.
1.newSkills: Staying awake longer, looking more attentively, a first real smile.
1.title: Sensations

10.description: A sense of self emerges — mine, yours, me. Moods swing widely.
10.newSkills: Naming themselves, playing pretend, following simple rules.
10.title: Systems

2.description: Shapes, sounds and movements start to fall into patterns. Hands and voice get discovered.
2.newSkills: Grasping deliberately, following things with the eyes, first cooing.
2.title: Patterns

3.description: Movements become less jerky. Many babies watch their surroundings much more closely.
3.newSkills: Turning the head towards sounds, rolling attempts, laughing out loud.
3.title: Smooth transitions

4.description: Sequences begin to make sense. Frustration grows because wanting outpaces being able.
4.newSkills: Reaching for things on purpose, passing them hand to hand, babbling in syllables.
4.title: Events

5.description: Distance becomes noticeable — and so does being apart. Stranger anxiety often starts here.
5.newSkills: Sitting freely, moving towards things, understanding simple words.
5.title: Relationships

6.description: Things get sorted: this belongs together, that does not. Curiosity gets very physical.
6.newSkills: Crawling, pulling up to stand, pointing at things.
6.title: Categories

7.description: One thing after another — stacking, filling, emptying. Imitation becomes a favourite game.
7.newSkills: First steps with support, first words, drinking from a cup.
7.title: Sequences

8.description: Whole routines are understood: eating, tidying up, going to bed.
8.newSkills: Walking freely, helping to undress, following short instructions.
8.title: Programmes

9.description: Testing what happens when. Boundaries get explored deliberately.
9.title: Principles

milestone.pincer: Picks things up with thumb and finger
milestone.walk-assisted: Walks holding a hand or furniture

milestones.note: The windows do not say when something should happen — they show the range in which healthy children take this step, and it is remarkably wide. Six of them (sitting alone, standing with support, crawling, walking with help, standing alone, walking alone) come from the WHO Motor Development Study; the rest are common experience.
milestones.title: Milestones

more.milestonesHint: Tick off what she can already do

region.label: Country
region.lead: Controls which check-ups and vaccination dates appear on the timeline. Applies to the whole household.
region.medicalNote: This does not replace medical advice — your paediatric practice sets the actual appointments.
region.noneHint: Without appointments the timeline shows leaps, photos and your own entries only.
region.unverified: These dates were gathered from public sources and are not officially verified. Please check them against your country's own schedule.

settings.appearanceAutoHint: dark in the evening, light by day
settings.appearanceLead: At night the app switches to a warm, muted look — bright, blue-tinted light at three in the morning makes falling back asleep needlessly hard.

childRejected.text: A value is out of range — usually birth length or head circumference. Please enter it in centimetres (e.g. 52) and save.
childRejected.title: The child details are not being synced

settings.confirmationsLead: The short messages after each entry. Failures and warnings still appear.
settings.confirmationsOffHint: The card at the top still updates straight away; undo lives in the history
settings.languageLead: Applies to this device only. Dates and times follow the chosen language.
settings.photosLead2: From the weekly photos the server builds a video in week order.

push.alsoAtNightHint: Around the clock — tap to switch.
push.denied: Notifications are blocked for this site in the browser. That can only be changed there, not in the app.
push.lead: Lets you know when the next bottle might be due — estimated from {name} own rhythm, not from a table. This setting applies to this device only.
push.needsInstall: On iPhone and iPad notifications only work when the app sits on the home screen — not in Safari itself. Use the share menu to “Add to Home Screen” and open the app from there.
push.note: A reminder, not an alarm: when she is really hungry is her call — the estimate is only the gap between past feeds.
push.quietAtNightHint: At night the child is the alarm clock anyway. Tap to switch.
push.serverDisabled: No keys are configured on the server. Without them nobody can be notified.
push.title: Bottle reminder

settings.signOutNote: Only clears the local copy on this phone. All entries stay on the server and on the other device.
settings.timelapseServer: The server could not build the video.
settings.timelapseTooFew: That needs at least two weekly photos.
settings.title: Settings
settings.weatherLead: With a location the server fetches the daily temperature once a day and puts it next to the intake. In hot weather she often drinks more — this way you can see why. Only coordinates leave the device, no data about the child.

setup.intro: These details drive the weeks of life, the timeline and the growth charts. All of it can be changed later in settings.
